new_candidates.body:
There are a few MuJoCo-specific parameters that do not map to physics params in SDF.  There are also parameters like friction where the values produce different results in MuJoCo vs other physics engines so it's desirable to make it clear that they are specific to MuJoCo.

## Desired behavior
Users can specify MuJoCo specific constraint solver and contact parameters like `solref`, `solimp`, `priority`, `impratio`, etc. One option is to include these params inside a custom `<gz:mujoco>` tag.


From @facontidavide

Some data for the discussion on passing MuJoCo parameters from SDF, from benchmarking a quadruped (ANYmal D, 57 kg, trotting with an effort controller) on gz-sim main with the MuJoCo plugin, against Gazebo Classic with ODE as the reference.

With the plugin's current settings, every contact runs on MuJoCo's defaults: a 20 ms constraint time constant (`solref`), 16 times our 1.25 ms step. Foot penetration (p99 over the trot) is 9.1 mm, against 0.86 mm with ODE, and stance slip is 2 to 4 times ODE's. To find out which parameters matter, I added temporary environment-variable overrides to the plugin and swept them (5 scenarios, 3 runs each):

| Setting | Penetration p99 | Slip p95 |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin defaults (solref 20 ms, solimp 0.9/0.95, pyramidal cone, friction 1) | 9.1 mm | 29.5 mm/s |
| friction 0.8 | 8.7 mm | 31.0 mm/s |
| solimp 0.95/0.99 | 8.5 mm | 25.0 mm/s |
| elliptic cone, impratio 10 | 8.9 mm | 16.5 mm/s |
| solref 5 ms | 1.6 mm | 14.9 mm/s |
| solref 2.5 ms (2x the step) | 0.37 mm | 12.0 mm/s |
| solref 2.5 ms, solimp 0.95/0.99, elliptic, impratio 10, friction 0.8 | 0.38 mm | 10.6 mm/s |
| ODE (reference) | 0.86 mm | 9.6 mm/s |

The time constant is what matters for penetration; the cone and `impratio` matter for slip once contact is stiff. With the last row the robot passes all our contact checks against ODE. These are MuJoCo's documented recommendations for stiff contact rather than a fit to this robot, but no SDF element reaches them today.

The soft default also matters for heightmaps. MuJoCo can pull a small object into a height field under soft contact (google-deepmind/mujoco#2883, which its maintainers call a flaw in height field collisions). I reproduced it in plain MuJoCo 3.11: a 2 cm box dropped 6 cm onto a height field comes to rest 16 to 21 mm lower than it should with the defaults, and on the surface with `solref` 2.5 ms.

So users need, per collision, `solref`, `solimp`, `friction` (all three MuJoCo coefficients) and `condim`, and per world, `cone` and `impratio` (and perhaps `noslip_iterations`). Building on @azeey's `<gz:mujoco>` idea, a block that uses MuJoCo's own names and units would let people carry values over from MJCF and the MuJoCo docs unchanged:

```xml
<collision name="foot">
  <surface>
    <gz:mujoco>
      <friction>0.8 0.005 0.0001</friction>
      <solref>0.0025 1</solref>
      <solimp>0.95 0.99 0.001</solimp>
      <condim>3</condim>
    </gz:mujoco>
  </surface>
</collision>

<physics name="1ms" type="mujoco">
  <gz:mujoco>
    <cone>elliptic</cone>
    <impratio>10</impratio>
  </gz:mujoco>
</physics>
```

When the block is absent the plugin would keep its current behavior, so nothing changes for existing worlds. The generic `<surface><friction>` values from this PR could still apply when `<gz:mujoco><friction>` isn't given.

## Alternatives considered

Add `<mujoco>` tag upstream in SDFormat along side of other physics engines like [`<ode>`](https://sdformat.org/spec/1.12/collision/#friction_ode) and [`<bullet>`](https://sdformat.org/spec/1.12/collision/#friction_bullet). However, this is no longer recommended, see https://github.com/gazebosim/sdformat/issues/508.

## Implementation suggestion



## Additional context
See comments in https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-physics/pull/1006 discussion on the need of mujoco specific parameters.

new_candidates.body:
### This is not a TF-synchronisation question

The TF failure in what follows is **expected, correct, and correctly detected**. The bug is what
`ControllerServer` does *after* it is detected: a transform failure is silently converted into a
goal-reached verdict. Filing because the fix already exists in `main` and was never backported.

(Adjacent but different: #5234 quotes the same three lines but asks why `transform_tolerance` is not
overridable, and #5227 is about TF sync. Neither reports the discarded return value.)

### The defect, in two halves

**Half one — `nav_2d_utils::transformPose` leaves `out_pose` untouched on failure**
(`nav2_dwb_controller/nav_2d_utils/src/tf_help.cpp`, humble):

```cpp
  } catch (tf2::ExtrapolationException & ex) {
    auto transform = tf->lookupTransform(frame, in_pose.header.frame_id, tf2::TimePointZero);
    if ((rclcpp::Time(in_pose.header.stamp) - rclcpp::Time(transform.header.stamp)) >
      transform_tolerance)
    {
      RCLCPP_ERROR(rclcpp::get_logger("tf_help"), "Transform data too old when converting from %s to %s", ...);
      return false;                     // out_pose NOT assigned
    } else {
      tf2::doTransform(in_pose, out_pose, transform);
      return true;
    }
  } catch (tf2::TransformException & ex) {
    RCLCPP_ERROR(rclcpp::get_logger("tf_help"), "Exception in transformPose: %s", ex.what());
    return false;                       // out_pose NOT assigned
  }
```

**Half two — `ControllerServer::isGoalReached()` discards that return**
(`nav2_controller/src/controller_server.cpp`, humble):

```cpp
  geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped transformed_end_pose;      // default-constructed: all zeros
  rclcpp::Duration tolerance(rclcpp::Duration::from_seconds(costmap_ros_->getTransformTolerance()));
  nav_2d_utils::transformPose(                                // return value DISCARDED
    costmap_ros_->getTfBuffer(), costmap_ros_->getGlobalFrameID(),
    end_pose_, transformed_end_pose, tolerance);

  return goal_checkers_[current_goal_checker_]->isGoalReached(
    pose.pose, transformed_end_pose.pose, velocity);
```

So on any failing tick the goal checker is handed **(0, 0, 0) in the costmap's global frame** as the
goal, and compares the live robot pose against it.

### Why that is a false success rather than a harmless miss

With the usual `local_costmap: global_frame: odom`, the origin of the compared frame is where
odometry started — so the fabricated goal sits at the robot's own odom origin. A robot near the
start of its odometry is therefore **within `xy_goal_tolerance` of a goal it never received**, and
`SimpleGoalChecker` returns true. `FollowPath` then reports `SUCCEEDED` without having driven the
path.

The distinguishing signature, if anyone wants to check their own logs: the distance between the
robot and the *compared* goal shrinks monotonically as odom drifts back through its origin, whereas
a real goal several metres away gives a near-constant distance. A `SUCCEEDED` whose
`xy_goal_tolerance` was never physically satisfied is the symptom.

### It is reachable in practice

From one of our runs (Isaac Sim, `nav2 1.1.20-1jammy`, RPP controller, ground-truth localizer
publishing `map→odom` at 20 Hz against 30 ms odometry):

```
[ERROR] [tf_help]: Transform data too old when converting from map to odom
[ERROR] [tf_help]: Data time: 15s 339999657ns, Transform time: 14s 109999684ns
```

Nine of those, logger `tf_help`, which is `nav_2d_utils::transformPose` returning **false** — the
exact call `isGoalReached()` ignores. (Attributed carefully: `Transform data too old` appears only in
`libtf_help.so`. The `Exception in transformPose` / `Unable to transform robot pose into global
plan's frame` pairs in the same log are the RPP path handler, which *does* check its return.)

We have separately seen a controller report success at a path fraction of 0.031, repeatedly, which
is consistent with this mechanism — stated as consistent-with, not as a proven chain.

### Already fixed in `main`

`ControllerServer::transformedPlanAndGoal()` now checks it and refuses:

```cpp
  if (!nav2_util::transformPoseInTargetFrame(
      end_pose_, transformed_end_pose_, *costmap_ros_->getTfBuffer(),
      costmap_ros_->getGlobalFrameID(), transform_tolerance_))
  {
    throw nav2_core::ControllerTFError("Failed to transform end pose to global frame");
  }
```

So the intended behaviour is settled upstream; `humble` simply never received it.

### Suggested minimal backport

```cpp
  if (!nav_2d_utils::transformPose(
      costmap_ros_->getTfBuffer(), costmap_ros_->getGlobalFrameID(),
      end_pose_, transformed_end_pose, tolerance))
  {
    return false;   // cannot locate the goal in this frame; not reached
  }
```

`isGoalReached()` already has a `return false` path for a missing robot pose immediately above, so
this is consistent with the method's existing failure handling and changes no behaviour on the
success path. Happy to open the PR against `humble` if that is wanted.

### Environment

- nav2 `1.1.20-1jammy` (`ros-humble-nav2-controller`, `ros-humble-nav2-util`), ROS 2 Humble, Ubuntu 22.04
- RPP controller, `local_costmap` `global_frame: odom`, `transform_tolerance: 0.3`
new_candidates.title: Humble: ControllerServer::isGoalReached() discards transformPose's return, comparing the robot against a default-constructed (0,0,0) goal (fixed in main, not backported)
